title: Pre-Analysis — Proposed Extension of the Aft Cargo Door Surround Splice Plate Reinforcement Beyond the ZEPHYR-24 Evo
abstract: Pre-analysis of a proposal to extend the thicker aft cargo door surround splice plates to earlier aircraft types, closed with a negative position after the load case and the published repair content were examined.

sections.objective: Test the proposal that the reinforced splice plate standard, released against a certification finding on one aircraft type, should be extended to the wider family. The proposal came from a maintenance organisation that had seen the reinforcement fitted and assumed it answered a cracking pattern it was also seeing on earlier aircraft. Pre-analysis was asked to establish whether the two findings are the same finding, and whether the reinforcement can be fitted at all to a door surround built to the earlier standard.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and the proposal did not survive them. The reinforcement was substantiated against a door closing effort and weight variant combination that exists only on the heavier aircraft type; the load case that drives the plate thickness is simply not present on the earlier build. More decisively, the published stringer splice repair for the cut-out corner is written against the earlier surround geometry and is embodied on a significant part of the fleet the proposal targets, and the reinforced plate cannot be installed over it without removing a repair that many operators would have to justify removing. The part list figure would need a third configuration for a population that does not need the change. A candidate insulation change in the same compartment would also have to be resequenced. The maintenance organisation's cracking pattern was referred back for a separate assessment.
sections.next_steps: Return a negative position to the originator with the load case argument written out, and make clear that the reinforcement is not a repair for the cracking pattern reported. Raise a separate in-service query against the reported cracking on the earlier build so that it is assessed on its own evidence rather than folded into this standard. No change is proposed to the released modification, its bulletin or its effectivity.

similarity_seeds: longitudinal splice plate reinforcement at a cargo door surround
stringer splice repair at a door cut-out corner
door closing effort on a high weight variant

tasks.title: Compare the substantiating load case with the earlier build standard
Search published repairs on the same door surround
Assess part list and effectivity consequences of a third configuration

expected_findings.rationale: The published stringer splice repair at the cut-out corner is embodied on a large share of the population the proposal targets. The reinforced plate lands on the repair doubler and cannot be installed over it, so extending the standard would oblige operators to remove a substantiated repair.
expected_findings.resolution: No action on the repair. The proposal is rejected rather than reworked around it.

expected_findings.rationale: The retrofit bulletin states a weight variant condition as well as an aircraft type condition. Extending the modification without extending that condition would produce a bulletin that contradicts its own accomplishment instructions.
expected_findings.resolution: None. The effectivity statement stays as issued.

expected_findings.rationale: The door structure figure already carries pre and post reinforcement sheets. A third configuration for a population that does not need the change would make the alternate item notation ambiguous for the aircraft that do.
expected_findings.resolution: None. Recorded so that the figure is not re-opened if the proposal returns.

expected_findings.rationale: The candidate blanket installation occupies the same compartment ceiling and sidewall access that the splice plate work needs. Had the extension gone ahead, the two would have had to be sequenced deliberately rather than left to the conversion centre.
expected_findings.resolution: None while the proposal is rejected; noted for the candidate's own pre-analysis.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares the aft fuselage secondary chapter, the same aircraft type and almost the same title vocabulary — a new attachment fitting standard driven by a design service goal — but it acts on the stabiliser front spar. There is no shared part number, no shared zone and no access overlap with the cargo door surround.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with a negative position. The reinforcement answers a load case that does not exist on the proposed population, and the published corner repair makes installation impractical on a large part of it.
